wave.title: Shortener MVP: links + click stats
wave.goal: A working URL shortener (create, redirect, count clicks) built under strict gates (format, lint, mypy strict, import-linter layers, coverage >= 90%) to test whether autonome implements within enforced limits.

discussion.text: Wave scope: only links and click-stats; out: auth, custom codes, expiration, delete/edit, rate limit, detailed stats. Agree?
Gates: ruff format --check, extra ruff rules (S, SIM, RET, ANN), mypy --strict, import-linter, coverage >= 90%, all block mode.

review_findings.issue: test_init_db_is_idempotent only calls init_db() twice and asserts nothing. It would be stronger to check the links table still exists after the second call.

_is_internal_host only catches literal addresses that ipaddress.ip_address parses in dotted-quad or colon form. Alternate IPv4 spellings such as http://2130706433/, http://0x7f.0.0.1/ and http://127.1/ are not parsed as IPs, so they are not flagged as internal and validate_url accepts them. The briefing scopes the check to what ipaddress recognises, so this is advisory. The service stores and redirects without fetching, which lowers the SSRF impact. Not verified by running code: the Bash tool was denied in this session.

create_link catches every sqlite3.IntegrityError and retries, not only a code collision. A non-code integrity failure (for example a NOT NULL violation) would be retried 5 times and then surface as a misleading RuntimeError about codes. Narrowing the catch to a primary-key conflict, or re-raising when the code is not the cause, would keep the retry to what the plan asks for.

connect() now passes check_same_thread=False. The briefing does not list db.py as a change. It is probably needed because the sync generator dependency and the endpoint can run on different threadpool threads, and the connection is never shared across concurrent requests, so it is safe. Still, it loosens a shared helper that the briefing did not mention. Mention it in the handoff.

create_link raises a bare RuntimeError after MAX_ATTEMPTS code collisions. A request that hits this becomes a raw 500, which the 'no path returns a raw 500' convention forbids. The chance is negligible with a 62^7 space, so this is advisory only.

features.title: Click stats: count redirects per link
features.rehearsal_notes: Plan #101 fits the code as it is now; no gate blocks it. I could not read autonome memory (plan_list was denied), so I checked the repo and git log instead; the links plan is merged (last commit 56acffe). Notes for implementers: (1) db.connect() takes no timeout argument; sqlite3's default 5s timeout is enough for the 100-write concurrency test, or add a timeout param to connect(), but do not call sqlite3.connect directly in the test. (2) init_db runs executescript(SCHEMA), so appending the clicks table with IF NOT EXISTS is safe on an existing links-only DB; foreign_keys is already ON in connect(), so the unknown-code IntegrityError case works. (3) stats needs only sqlite3 and datetime, which the layers and forbidden contracts allow; it does not need db, links or any web package. (4) The count column name is valid SQLite; SQL strings are constant with parameters, so ruff S rules pass; strict mypy needs annotations in test thread helpers. (5) /links/{code}/stats has two segments, so it cannot clash with GET /{code}; declaring it first is harmless. (6) stats.py is currently a docstring-only stub; replace its docstring when adding code.

review_findings.issue: get_stats reads columns by position (row[0]..row[4]), while links.get_link in the same layer reads them by name (row["code"]) on the sqlite3.Row factory set by db.connect(). Named access would match the layer's style and survive a column reorder in the SELECT.

tasks.title: Record clicks on redirect and GET /links/{code}/stats

review_findings.issue: redirect() now calls stats.record_click() before returning. If that write fails (for example sqlite3.OperationalError 'database is locked' after the 5s default timeout under concurrent redirects), the request ends in a raw 500 instead of a JSON error. The convention says no path returns a raw 500. Advisory only: the acceptance does not name this case, and the write path is simple.

tune:
Propus 3 convenções e 1 plano. Tudo fica pendente até você aprovar na UI.

1. **Convenção 157 (process):** usar Edit/Write e só `uv run`, e rodar os gates antes de terminar. O Bash foi negado em 9 dos 10 handoffs, e os agentes terminaram com "not verified" (122, 125, 129, 133, 140, 143, 153, 118, 137).
2. **Convenção 158 (process):** ler o briefing primeiro e listar os arquivos alterados fora dele. Em 7 handoffs não aparece leitura do briefing (122, 133, 140, 148, 153, 118, 137). A task 115 mexeu no `db.py` sem o briefing mandar.
3. **Convenção 159 (api, persistence, test):** falha de banco vira erro JSON, captura estreita da exceção, com teste. Os achados de review das tasks 114, 115 e 117 quebraram a convenção 103 (sem 500 cru). O handoff 143 mostra um bug de thread que passou por todos os gates.
4. **Plano 160 (process):** dois testes no gate pytest que já existe, sem gate novo. Um cobre falha de banco por endpoint, o outro cobre requisições concorrentes.

Deixei de fora o achado das grafias alternativas de IPv4 (task 113), porque apareceu só uma vez. Nenhuma convenção existente foi afrouxada.
